requested_parts: Escape Pod count for four players
Pod section distribution and starting orientation
Initial Intruder bag contents
answers.answer: 1. Select 3 Escape Pod tokens. 2. Put the lowest-numbered Pod in Section A, the next in B, then alternate A/B; all begin Locked side up. 3. Put 1 Blank, 4 Larvae, 1 Creeper, 1 Queen, 3 Adults, and 1 additional Adult per player in the bag. With four players, that is 7 Adults and 14 tokens total.
answers.evidence: 1–2 players: 2 pods; 3–4 players: 3 pods; 5 players: 4 pods. Place the lowest-numbered pod in Section "A", the next (in numerical order) in Section "B", then alternate A/B. All pods start with their Locked side face up. For each player count, put these Intruder tokens in the Intruder bag: 1 Blank, 4 Larvae, 1 Creeper, 1 Queen, 3 Adults, plus 1 additional Adult per player. Inference for four players: 3 fixed Adults + 4 additional Adults = 7 Adults; total tokens are 1 + 4 + 1 + 1 + 7 = 14.

requested_parts: Filter and deal the Objective cards
Timing and choice of the retained Objective
Disposition of the rejected Objective
Whether Eggs trigger the choice
answers.answer: 1. Let P be the actual player count; remove from each Objective deck every card requiring more than P players, shuffle Corporate and Personal decks separately, then deal each player one of each face down/hidden. 2. Players choose one of their two Objectives at the First Encounter, when the first Intruder miniature appears, before the Encounter is resolved. 3. Remove the rejected card face down from the game; nobody may look at another player's removed Objective. 4. Eggs do not trigger this choice because they are not Intruders.
answers.evidence: Let P be the actual number of players in this game. Remove from both Objective decks (Corporate and Personal) every card requiring more than P players. Shuffle the two decks separately and deal each player 1 Corporate and 1 Personal Objective card, kept hidden. The first time an Intruder miniature (of any type) appears on the board, every player immediately chooses 1 of their 2 Objective cards and removes the other from the game face down (unseen by anyone — players may never look at others' removed Objectives). Then the triggering Encounter is resolved. Eggs are not Intruders and do not trigger this.

requested_parts: Cards discarded to pay and use the cost-2 Action card
Whether Contamination cards can substitute for payment
How to resolve an Action card with OR effects
answers.answer: 1. Discard the played Action card plus two other Action cards: three Action cards total. The two Contamination cards stay in hand and cannot pay the cost. 2. No: Contamination cards are not Action cards and cannot be discarded for an Action cost. 3. Choose one of the card's OR sections; the card does not resolve both alternatives.
answers.evidence: Each Action's icon shows a number — discard exactly that many Action cards from your hand (face up) to pay. For an Action card, also discard the card you play: printed cost n requires n + 1 Action cards in total. Contamination cards are not Action cards: they can never be discarded to pay any Action cost. Each Character has a partially unique deck of 10 Action cards. To use one, discard that card face up and pay its cost by discarding the required number of additional Action cards. If a card has two sections separated by "OR," choose one.

requested_parts: Timing of the Fire wound after taking one Action and passing
Whether the player may take another normal Action this Player Phase
Whether cards may be discarded when passing
Whether later players' rounds cause further Fire wounds
answers.answer: 1. The Character takes 1 Light Wound at the end of their own round in the burning Room, after taking the one Action and passing. 2. They cannot take further normal Actions after passing, though the summary notes the separate Interruption exception. 3. At the moment of passing, they may discard any number of hand cards. 4. No: they take the Fire wound once at the end of their own passing round, not during later players' rounds.
answers.evidence: A Character who ends their round in a Room with a Fire marker suffers 1 Light Wound (every round; only after finishing their own round — passing players take it once at the end of their round and no more that turn). After you pass: You cannot take further normal Actions; Interruption remains permitted as below. At the moment you pass, you may discard any number of cards from your hand. Later players' rounds do not give you further Fire wounds that turn.

requested_parts: Room tile and Exploration token resolution on entry
Item Counter handling and Exploration-token destination
Exploration effects that replace the ordinary Noise roll
Ordinary Noise roll condition and resolution
Silence, Danger, and an already-occupied destination effects on Noise
answers.answer: 1. On entering an empty unexplored Room, flip its tile face up and reveal and resolve its Exploration token. 2. For the Item Counter, rotate the Room tile until the Exploration token's number faces the Item Counter symbol printed on the board; the Nest and Room Covered With Slime get no Item count. After resolving the effect, remove the Exploration token from the game into the box. 3. Silence or Danger replaces the Movement Noise roll, so do not roll again afterward. 4. Otherwise, because the destination is empty, make the ordinary Noise roll and resolve it. 5. Silence produces no marker (unless the mover has Slime, when it becomes Danger); Danger moves all eligible neighboring Intruders in, or if none are eligible places Noise in every connected Corridor without a marker. If any Character or Intruder is already in the destination, do not make the ordinary Movement Noise roll.
answers.evidence: After entering a Room: (1) if the Room tile was unexplored (face down), flip it face up and reveal and resolve its Exploration token, then return that token to the box (removed from the game); (2) apply the Movement Noise rule. A Silence or Danger Exploration result replaces the Movement Noise roll: resolve that result and do not roll Noise again afterward. Otherwise, perform the ordinary Noise roll if the destination is empty (no Characters, no Intruders). If anyone — Character or Intruder — is already there, do NOT roll for Movement Noise. The Nest and Room Covered With Slime get no Item count. For other Room tiles, rotate the tile until the Exploration token's number faces the Item Counter symbol printed on the board next to the slot. Silence — no Movement Noise roll. Nothing happens. If your Character has a Slime marker, resolve "Danger" instead. Danger — no Movement Noise roll. Move ALL eligible Intruders from neighboring Rooms into this Room (eligible means not in Combat with any Character). If there are none eligible, place a Noise marker in every Corridor connected to this Room that lacks one, counting Technical Corridors if the Room has an Entrance. After resolving an Exploration token, remove it from the game into the box; it does not return to a supply or stay on the Room (each is resolved only once, on first entry).

requested_parts: Careful Movement Action-card cost
What Careful Movement replaces and where its Noise marker goes
When Careful Movement is forbidden
Whether a Closed Door may be crossed
Whether a miniature can stop in a Corridor
answers.answer: 1. Careful Movement costs 2 Action cards. 2. Instead of rolling Noise after moving, place a Noise marker in a chosen Corridor connected to the destination Room; it also replaces automatic Silence/Danger Exploration results with that chosen placement. 3. It cannot be used in Combat or when every Corridor connected to the destination already has a Noise marker. 4. No: normal Movement restrictions apply, and a Closed Door blocks passage. 5. No miniature may stop in a Corridor; characters and Intruders occupy Rooms (with Escape Pods the stated Character exception).
answers.evidence: Careful Movement (cost 2) — follows normal Movement restrictions, including Closed Doors blocking passage; but instead of a Noise roll after moving, place a Noise marker in a chosen Corridor connected to the Room you enter. You cannot Carefully Move if all Corridors connected to the destination already hold Noise markers, and you cannot use it while in Combat. The FAQ clarifies that Careful Movement also replaces automatic Silence/Danger Exploration results with its chosen Noise placement; Reconnaissance cancels those automatic results too. Characters and Intruders may only occupy Rooms (Special Rooms — Hibernatorium, Cockpit, Engines — count as Rooms; Escape Pod tokens are the only exception for Characters). Corridors connect Rooms; no one may ever stop in a Corridor.

requested_parts: Resolution when a Noise roll selects a Corridor already holding Noise
Placement of Noise for a Technical Corridors Entrance and the shared-marker rule
Encounter sequence and removal of connected Noise markers
Surprise Attack hand-size comparison and card types counted
answers.answer: 1. A roll of 1–4 selects the correspondingly numbered connected Corridor; if that Corridor already has Noise, resolve an Encounter instead of placing a second marker. 2. For a Technical Corridors Entrance, place the Noise marker on the single Technical Corridors space; that marker applies to every Technical Corridors Entrance, and a second marker there likewise causes an Encounter. 3. For the Encounter, discard all Noise markers from all Corridors connected to the Room, including Technical Corridors if it has an Entrance; draw a token, keep a non-Blank token outside the bag, and place its matching Intruder miniature. A Blank follows its separate procedure and creates no miniature. 4. Compare the number on the token with the triggering player's hand: fewer cards than the number causes a Surprise Attack against that player; equal or more causes no attack. Both Action and Contamination cards count toward hand size.
answers.evidence: Result 1, 2, 3, or 4: place a Noise marker in the Corridor with that number connected to the Room you entered (counting Technical Corridors if the Room has an Entrance). A Corridor may never hold more than 1 Noise marker — if instructed to place a marker where one already is, resolve an Encounter instead. If a Noise marker's number leads to a Technical Corridors Entrance, place the marker on the Technical Corridors space. A Noise marker there is treated as if it were in every Technical Corridors Entrance on the whole board. The 1-marker limit applies: placing a second one there resolves an Encounter instead. Discard ALL Noise markers from all Corridors connected to the Room (including Technical Corridors if there's an Entrance). Draw 1 Intruder token from the bag (symbol on one side, number on the other). Keep a non-Blank token aside outside the bag; it is not immediately returned. A Blank follows its separate return procedure below. Place the matching Intruder miniature in the Room. Compare the token's number to the number of cards in the triggering player's hand (Action AND Contamination cards both count). Fewer cards than the number → Surprise Attack (an Intruder Attack against that Character). Equal or more → nothing happens.

requested_parts: Danger resolution with one or more eligible neighboring Intruders
Danger resolution when no neighboring Intruder is eligible
Whether an Intruder moving into a Character's Room is an Encounter
Slime's effect on Silence
answers.answer: 1. Move all eligible Intruders from neighboring Rooms into the Room; eligible means not in Combat with any Character. 2. If there are none eligible, place a Noise marker in every connected Corridor that lacks one, including Technical Corridors when the Room has an Entrance. 3. No: an Intruder merely moving into a Character's Room is not an Encounter; it is simply Combat. 4. If the Character has Slime, a Silence result resolves as Danger instead.
answers.evidence: Danger — no Movement Noise roll. Move ALL eligible Intruders from neighboring Rooms into this Room (eligible means not in Combat with any Character). If there are none eligible, place a Noise marker in every Corridor connected to this Room that lacks one, counting Technical Corridors if the Room has an Entrance. An Intruder merely moving into a Room with a Character is NOT an Encounter (they are simply in Combat). Silence — no Movement Noise roll. Nothing happens. If your Character has a Slime marker, resolve "Danger" instead.

requested_parts: Blank token outcome during an Encounter, including Noise placement and token return
When an Adult is added after an Encounter Blank
Blank token outcome during bag development
answers.answer: 1. During an Encounter, a Blank causes a Noise marker to be placed in each Corridor connected to the Room; the Encounter ends without a miniature appearing, and the Blank returns to the bag. 2. Add 1 Adult to the bag only if the Blank was the last token in the bag, and only if an Adult token is available. 3. In bag development, a Blank adds 1 Adult token if one is available, then the Blank is returned to the bag; this branch does not require the Blank to have been the last token.
answers.evidence: Blank token in an Encounter: place a Noise marker in each Corridor connected to that Room. If the Blank was the LAST token in the bag: add 1 Adult token to the bag (if any are available; otherwise nothing). Return the Blank token to the bag. The Encounter ends (no miniature appears). Blank — add 1 Adult Intruder token to the bag (if none are available, nothing happens). Return the Blank token to the bag.

requested_parts: Where two Intruders moving together through a Closed Door end up and what happens to the Door
Whether the Door can later be closed again
Whether a Noise-triggered appearance is blocked by a Closed Door
answers.answer: 1. Neither Intruder moves through the Closed Door: both stay in their original Room, and the Door is destroyed (the token is laid down). 2. Yes, but only the Plasma Torch Item can close a Destroyed Door; other Door-closing effects cannot. 3. No: an Intruder appearing because of a Noise roll comes through a Corridor with a Closed Door regardless of the Door.
answers.evidence: Closed = standing token: blocks Character and Intruder movement (and Grenade throws). An Intruder trying to move through a Closed Door does not move — it destroys the Door instead (several Intruders moving from the same Room destroy it simultaneously and all stay put). Destroyed = lying token: movement allowed; only the Plasma Torch Item can Close a Destroyed Door. Other Door-closing effects cannot Close it. If a Noise roll causes an Intruder to come through a Corridor with a Closed Door, it appears regardless of the Door.

requested_parts: What happens to the injured Intruder miniature when it moves into Technical Corridors
What happens to its Injury markers and token
Whether Noise on the Technical Corridors space is removed
Whether Characters and Door tokens can normally use Technical Corridors
answers.answer: 1. The Intruder disappears into the ducts and its miniature is removed from the board. 2. Discard all its Injury markers and return its Intruder token to the bag. 3. No: a Noise marker on the Technical Corridors space is not removed. 4. Characters cannot use Technical Corridors except through the Mechanic's Technical Corridors Action card or Technical Corridor Plans Item card, and Door tokens can never be placed there.
answers.evidence: If an Intruder moves to a Technical Corridors Entrance, it disappears into the ducts: discard all its Injury markers, return its token to the Intruder bag, and remove its miniature from the board. A Noise marker on the Technical Corridors space is NOT removed by this. Some Rooms have Technical Corridors Entrances, all linked to the single Technical Corridors space. Characters can never use them (the only exceptions: the Mechanic's "Technical Corridors" Action card and the "Technical Corridor Plans" Item card). Door tokens can never be placed in Technical Corridors.

requested_parts: Action-card costs and Shoot's Ammo cost
Target location for Shoot and Melee
Whether Melee adds Contamination
Miss outcomes for Shoot and Melee
Damage on a two-hit die result
answers.answer: 1. Each Action costs 1 Action card; Shoot additionally requires a Weapon in Hand and discarding 1 Ammo from it. 2. Each targets one Intruder in your Room. 3. Melee draws 1 Contamination card and puts it on top of your Action discard pile; Shoot does not have that Melee draw. 4. A Shoot miss inflicts 0 Injuries and no Wound on the shooter; a Melee miss inflicts 0 Injuries and gives the attacker 1 Serious Wound. 5. A double-hit result deals 2 Injuries with Shoot but only 1 Injury in Melee.
answers.evidence: Shoot (cost 1 Action card + 1 Ammo) — attack an Intruder in your Room with a Weapon in your Hand, discarding 1 Ammo from that Weapon's card. Melee Attack (cost 1): (1) draw 1 Contamination card and put it on top of your Action discard pile; (2) choose 1 target Intruder in your Room; (3) roll the Combat die. Results mirror Shooting with two changes: any miss also inflicts 1 Serious Wound on your Character, and the 2-Injury result deals only 1 Injury (in melee, rolls of 2 Hits are treated as 1 Hit). A Shoot miss deals 0 Injuries to the target and causes no Wound to the shooter. A Melee miss deals 0 Injuries and causes 1 Serious Wound to the attacker. Double-hit symbol: 2 Injuries to any Intruder type before Weapon modifiers for Shoot; 1 Injury to any Intruder type for Melee.

requested_parts: How a Larva's death is checked and whether it leaves a Carcass
How an Adult's death is checked and when a Carcass is placed
How a Queen's death is checked and when a Carcass is placed
What a Retreat arrow during the Queen's check does
answers.answer: 1. A Larva dies from 1 Injury; remove its miniature and place no Carcass. 2. For an Adult, draw 1 Intruder Attack card and compare its blood value to the Intruder's current total Injuries: blood less than or equal to Injuries kills it; otherwise it remains alive. On death remove the miniature and place a Carcass in the Room. 3. For a Queen, draw 2 Attack cards and sum their blood values; a sum less than or equal to current Injuries kills it, otherwise it remains alive. On death remove the miniature and place a Carcass in the Room. 4. If either card drawn for the Queen shows a Retreat arrow, resolve retreat instead of numerical death/endurance: the Queen flees by drawing an Event card and moving through the Corridor number on its Intruder movement section, then discard that Event card.
answers.evidence: After any Injuries, put that many Injury markers on the Intruder's base and check its Injury Effect. Compare current total Injuries, not just the latest hit. Larva: 1 Injury kills; remove miniature; no Carcass. Adult: Draw 1 Intruder Attack card; use only its blood value. Blood ≤ Injuries kills; higher means alive. On death remove miniature; place Carcass in Room. Queen: Draw 2 Attack cards and sum blood values. Sum ≤ Injuries kills; higher means alive. On death remove miniature; place Carcass in Room. During an Injury Effect check, if any drawn card's blood icon contains the Retreat arrow, resolve retreat instead of a numerical endurance/death result. The Intruder flees: draw an Event card and move the Intruder through the Corridor whose number appears in that card's Intruder movement section, then discard that Event card. The Queen and Breeders retreat if EITHER of their 2 drawn cards shows the Retreat symbol.

requested_parts: When the Escape attacks occur, how many, and their order
Who is targeted by those attacks
What happens if the Character dies during Escape
What happens if the Character survives and reaches an empty unexplored Room
answers.answer: 1. Before moving, resolve one Intruder Attack for each of the two Intruders in the current Room, starting with the larger type (Queen, Breeder, Adult, Larva). 2. The attacks target the escaper. 3. If the Character dies, their Corpse stays in the Room they tried to leave. 4. If they survive, complete the move into the neighboring Room; because it is unexplored, reveal and resolve its tile and Exploration token, then make a Noise roll because the destination is empty unless the Exploration result replaces that roll.
answers.evidence: To leave a Room containing Intruders, perform a Movement Action (cost 1) to a neighboring Room (explored or unexplored). BEFORE moving, resolve an Intruder Attack — one separate Attack per Intruder in the Room, starting with the larger ones (Queen, Breeder, Adult, Larva; FAQ Rules 5). If you survive, complete the move (Noise roll if the destination is empty; explore normally if unexplored). If you die, your Corpse stays in the Room you tried to Escape from. An Escape attack targets the escaper. After entering a Room: (1) if the Room tile was unexplored (face down), flip it face up and reveal and resolve its Exploration token, then return that token to the box (removed from the game); (2) apply the Movement Noise rule. A Silence or Danger Exploration result replaces the Movement Noise roll: resolve that result and do not roll Noise again afterward. Otherwise, perform the ordinary Noise roll if the destination is empty (no Characters, no Intruders).

requested_parts: How the target of an ordinary Intruder Attack is selected among several Characters
How ties are broken
How a non-Larva attack hits or misses
Larva attack procedure and Contamination destination
answers.answer: 1. Among Characters in the Room, the Intruder targets the one whose player has the fewest Action cards in hand. 2. On a tie, choose the Character with the First Player token, or the next player in turn order. 3. For a non-Larva Intruder, draw 1 Intruder Attack card: resolve its effect only if its symbol matches the attacking Intruder's type; otherwise it misses. Ignore the blood icon during attacks and discard the card to the Intruder Attack discard pile. 4. A Larva draws no Attack card: remove its miniature from the board and place it on the target's Character board; the target gains 1 Contamination card on top of their Action discard pile. If the target already has a Larva, the attacking Larva disappears, the existing Larva stays, and the Character only gains the Contamination card; this attack does not automatically kill them.
answers.evidence: Choose the target: the Intruder attacks a Character in its Room — with several Characters present, the one whose player has the FEWEST Action cards in hand; on a tie, the Character with the First Player token (or the next player in turn order). For other Intruders, draw 1 Intruder Attack card: if it shows a symbol matching the attacking Intruder's type, resolve the card's effect; otherwise the attack misses. Ignore the blood icon during attacks. Discard the card to the Intruder Attack discard pile; if the deck runs out, reshuffle the discard pile into a new deck. A Larva does not draw Attack cards. Instead: remove the Larva miniature from the board and place it on the target's Character board (on the miniature picture), and the target gains 1 Contamination card. If the target already has a Larva, the attacking Larva disappears, the existing one stays, and the Character only gains the Contamination card; this attack does not automatically kill them (FAQ Rules 12). When a Character "gets a Contamination card," draw it from the Contamination deck and place it on top of their Action discard pile.

requested_parts: Whether dressing one Serious Wound prevents death from another Wound at three Serious Wounds
What happens when a third Light Wound is suffered
What Heal removes
Where the Corpse and Heavy Objects go on death
answers.answer: 1. No. A dressed Serious Wound still counts toward the three-wound limit, and at three Serious Wounds any additional Light or Serious Wound causes death. 2. On the third Light Wound, clear the Light Wound track and suffer a Serious Wound. 3. Heal removes a Light Wound or discards a Dressed Serious Wound card, as the healing effect specifies; it does not remove an undressed Serious Wound. 4. On death place a Character Corpse token in the Room and drop all Heavy Objects there.
answers.evidence: On a 3rd [Light Wound], clear the track and suffer a Serious Wound. A Character with 3 Serious Wounds dies instantly upon suffering ANY additional Wound (Light or Serious). Remove the miniature, place a Character Corpse token in the Room (now a Character Corpse Object), and drop all their Heavy Objects there. Dress a Serious Wound: flip the card face down — its effect is ignored, but it still counts toward the 3-wound limit. Dressing does not prevent death from a further Wound when you already have 3 Serious Wounds. Heal: remove a Light Wound or discard a Dressed Serious Wound card, as the healing effect specifies.

requested_parts: Canteen/Shower scan scope and treatment of scanned cards
How Canteen/Shower handle an Infected card with and without an existing Larva
Surgery scan scope and which cards it removes
Surgery's Larva removal, cost, and turn/hand consequence
answers.answer: 1. Canteen and Shower optionally scan all Contamination cards in the Character's hand, removing scanned non-Infected cards from the game and keeping Infected cards. 2. An Infected result places a Larva if none was already present; with a Larva already present, the Character dies and a Creeper is placed in the death Room. 3. Surgery scans all Contamination cards in the deck, hand, and discard pile, then removes all Infected cards from the game. 4. Surgery also removes a Larva if present, then causes 1 Light Wound and an automatic pass; shuffle all cards, including the entire hand and remaining Contamination cards, into the Action deck, leaving the hand empty until the next turn. The summary gives no Action-card cost for Surgery beyond its ordinary Room Action cost.
answers.evidence: For the optional Canteen/Shower hand scan: Non-Infected — remove the scanned non-Infected card from the game; no Larva from that result. Infected, no Larva already on board — keep the Infected card; place a Larva on Character board. Infected, Larva already on board — keep the Infected card; Character dies; place 1 Creeper in the death Room. Canteen: you may Scan all Contamination cards in your HAND and remove all non-Infected ones (an Infected result places a Larva on your board — with a Larva already there, you die and a Creeper appears in your Room). Shower Room: you may Scan all Contamination cards in your HAND and remove all non-Infected ones (Infected → Larva, as in the Canteen). Surgery: Scan ALL your Contamination cards (deck, hand, discard); remove all Infected ones; remove a Larva from your board if present. Then suffer 1 Light Wound and automatically pass, shuffling all your cards (including the entire hand and remaining Contamination cards) into your Action deck. Your hand stays empty until the next turn. Room Actions cost 2 Action cards.

requested_parts: Egg destruction by Shoot/Melee, Grenade, Molotov, and Fire
Melee penalties waived or retained against Eggs
Timing and location of Noise rolls after attempts
When and how the Nest is destroyed
answers.answer: 1. Each Injury from Shoot or Melee destroys 1 uncarried Egg; a Grenade destroys 2 Eggs; a Molotov destroys 1 Egg immediately, and its Fire marker can destroy Eggs in later Fire Damage steps. Fire normally destroys 1 uncarried Egg in every Event Phase Fire Damage step; for the Nest's Egg pool, Vulnerability to Fire raises this to 2 each step. 2. Successful Egg Melee still draws 1 Contamination card onto the Action discard pile. On a missed Egg Melee, neither Contamination nor a Wound applies; the summary says timing of the normal pre-roll draw in this miss exception is unresolved. 3. Roll Noise after every single Shoot, Melee, Grenade, or Molotov attempt, including a miss; for a remote Grenade/Molotov, roll in your own Room. 4. When no Eggs remain in the Nest (all carried away or destroyed), the Nest is destroyed and marked with 1 Injury marker.
answers.evidence: Shoot or Melee: Each Injury destroys 1 Egg. Resolve the normal attack, with the Egg Melee exception below. Grenade: Destroys 2 Eggs. Uncarried Eggs permit the Room to be targeted as if an Intruder were there. Molotov Cocktail: Destroys 1 Egg immediately; its Fire marker can continue destroying Eggs in later Fire Damage steps. Fire marker: Normally destroys 1 uncarried Egg during every Event Phase Fire Damage step. For the Nest's Egg pool, Vulnerability to Fire increases this to 2 per step (FAQ Rooms 7). A successful Egg Melee retains the normal draw of 1 Contamination card onto your Action discard pile. A missed Egg Melee causes neither Contamination nor a Wound. The manuals do not specify how to reconcile the normal pre-roll Contamination step with this miss exception; no refund or alternative draw timing is specified. After every single Shoot, Melee, Grenade or Molotov attempt to destroy an Egg, perform a Noise roll, including a miss. For a remote Grenade/Molotov, roll in your own Room, not the Nest (FAQ Rooms 2). Egg tokens on the Intruder board represent the Eggs in the Nest; taking or destroying Eggs removes them from the Intruder board. When no Eggs remain (all carried away or destroyed), the Nest is destroyed — mark it with 1 Injury marker.

requested_parts: Escape Pod entry prerequisites and payment
What must be resolved before entry and what prevents entry
Pod Character capacity and Heavy Object capacity
Available options after boarding and the consequences of waiting
answers.answer: 1. In the corresponding Section A or B Room, pay 2 Action cards for its Room Action; the Pod must be unlocked and have a free Character space. 2. You cannot enter if the Section contains an Intruder or Malfunction. First roll Noise; if an Intruder appears or reaches the Section, entry fails. 3. A Pod holds 2 Characters; Heavy Objects use no Character space. 4. After boarding, you may launch immediately. If you wait, you pass the current turn and are treated as present in the Section for bag-development Noise rolls. At the start of your first round in each later Player Phase, choose to wait and pass, launch, or exit freely into the Section Room and take a full round of 2 Actions. While waiting, an Intruder appearing in the Section returns every Character in any Pod there to the Section Room; a new boarder may immediately launch both occupants; a Malfunction leaves your wait/launch/exit choices available but blocks new Pod entry.
answers.evidence: Board: pay 2 Action cards for the corresponding Evacuation Section A/B Room Action. A Pod there must be Unlocked with a free Character space. No entry while the Section contains an Intruder or Malfunction. First roll Noise; an Intruder appearing or reaching the Section makes entry fail. Capacity: 2 Characters per Pod. Heavy Objects take no Character space. After boarding you may launch. Remove the Pod token and its occupants' miniatures from the game; they stop participating and count as arriving on Earth. They still face the final Contamination and Objective checks. Choosing to wait makes you pass the current turn, while you remain treated as present in the Section for bag-development Noise rolls (FAQ Rules 1). At the start of your first round in each later Player Phase, choose wait and pass, launch, or exit free into the Section Room and play a full round of 2 Actions (FAQ Rules 2–3). If an Intruder appears in the Section, every Character in any of its Pods immediately returns to the Section Room; if another Character boards your Pod, that new boarder may immediately launch both occupants; if a Malfunction appears, your normal wait/launch/exit choices remain available and only new entry is blocked.

requested_parts: Order of final checks
Outcome with two Damaged Engines
Outcome of a non-Earth destination, including the Quarantine/Mars exception
Contamination check for an Infected survivor or a survivor with a Larva
Whether Escape Pod passengers undergo the Contamination check
answers.answer: 1. Resolve Engines, then Coordinates, then Contamination, then Objectives. 2. If the ship has survived to the Engine check, two or three Damaged Engines make it explode; everything aboard dies, including hibernating Characters and Intruders, while launched Pod passengers are already away. 3. A non-Earth destination kills hibernating Characters if the ship is not destroyed; Intruders remain alive. A sleeper with the Quarantine Objective survives if the destination is Mars. 4. If any Contamination card scans Infected, or the Character already has a Larva, shuffle all Action and Contamination cards from deck, hand, and discard into one Action deck and draw the top 4; any Contamination among those four kills regardless of whether it is Infected, while four Action cards means the Character survives this check. A Character with a Larva skips the initial scan but still performs that shuffle and draw. If there is no Larva, first scan every Contamination card in the Action deck, hand, and discard; if none is Infected, there is no four-card draw. 5. Yes. Every surviving Character, including Escape Pod passengers, faces the Contamination check.
answers.evidence: Resolve Engines → Coordinates → Contamination → Objectives in that order. Engines, only if the ship has survived: reveal all three top Engine tokens. 2 or 3 Damaged Engines make the ship explode. EVERYTHING aboard dies, including hibernating Characters and Intruders. answers.evidence: Room Covered With Slime — no Action: entering automatically gives you a Slime marker before resolving its Exploration token, so a Silence token resolves as Danger (no Item count is set here; Malfunction markers can never be placed here; no Search Action). Slime marker: while on your board, every "Silence" result (Noise roll or Exploration token) becomes "Danger." Max 1 (further Slime does nothing). Removed by the Clothes Item or the Shower Room Action. Shower Room — discard your Slime marker; you may also Scan all Contamination cards in your HAND and remove all non-Infected ones (Infected → Larva, as in the Canteen). Fire can exist here normally and is NOT removed by showering.

requested_parts: What the Cockpit lets the player learn

answers.answer: 1. Check Coordinates lets you secretly look at the Coordinates card; you may lie, then replace it and remember it. 2. Set Destination moves the Destination marker. That marker selects one of four destination entries on the Coordinates card; when checking where the ship jumps, read the entry matching the marker's track space. 3. Coordinate information is private. 4. You cannot Set Destination with an Intruder in the Cockpit, and you cannot change Destination once anyone has hibernated. As a Room Action, Cockpit use also requires being there, outside Combat, and no Malfunction.
answers.evidence: Cockpit — Check Coordinates (secretly look at the Coordinates card; you may lie; replace it and remember it) OR Set Destination (move the Destination marker). The marker selects one of the four destination entries on the Coordinates card: read the entry corresponding to its track space when checking where the ship will jump. You can never Set Destination with an Intruder in the Cockpit, or change Destination once anyone is hibernating. Common requirements for every Room Action below: your Character must be in the Room whose Action you use, outside Combat, and the Room must have no Malfunction marker. Pay 2 Action cards.

requested_parts: How checking an Engine works and what may remain secret

You need not say whether you repaired it, but must say if you changed their order. 3. No prior check is required. 4. Repair/Break works even if the Engine Room has a Malfunction marker.
answers.evidence: Engines #1–#3 — Check the Engine (secretly look at the TOP token; you may lie). Repair/Break Engine (via a Repairs Action or Tools Item): secretly examine both tokens and restack them in any order — you needn't say whether you repaired it, but you MUST say if you changed the order. Works even with a Malfunction marker and without checking first.

requested_parts: When hibernation is legal and its required location, payment, and room conditions

Whether a later Hibernatorium Malfunction wakes or harms sleepers

Roll Noise; if an Intruder reaches or appears in the Room, the attempt fails. 3. Otherwise remove the Character miniature from the board; the Character stops participating until the end checks. 4. Once anyone hibernates, no Character may change Destination or initiate Self-Destruct; Coolant Leak can still start Self-Destruct as an Event. 5. No: a later Malfunction in the Hibernatorium does not wake or harm sleepers.

Hibernatorium — Try to hibernate: pay 2 Action cards while present, with Time on a blue space, no Intruder and no Malfunction in the Room. Roll Noise; an Intruder reaching/appearing in the Room makes the attempt fail. Otherwise remove your miniature and stop participating until the end checks. Once anyone hibernates, no one may change Destination or initiate Self-Destruct as a Character; Coolant Leak Event remains an exception. A later Hibernatorium Malfunction does not wake/harm sleepers.

requested_parts: What happens when Time reaches its final space

If the last alive, non-hibernating Character on board dies, hibernates, or launches in a Pod, the game ends: if Self-Destruct was active, move its marker to its final red space; otherwise move the Time marker to its final red space, and resolve that effect. 3. Thus active Self-Destruct causes the ship to explode and kills all Characters aboard, awake or hibernating, and everything else aboard, including Intruders. 4. Intruders are unharmed by a normal hyperspace jump.
answers.evidence: The Time marker reaches the final red space of the Time Track — the ship jumps to hyperspace immediately; every Character on board who is not hibernating dies from g-force. Intruders are unharmed by the hyperjump. The Self-Destruct marker reaches the final red ("skull") space of its Track — the ship explodes / loses hull integrity: ALL Characters on board (awake and hibernated) die, and everything else aboard dies too, including Intruders. The last alive, non-hibernating Character on board dies, hibernates, or launches in an Escape Pod. Then: if the Self-Destruct sequence was active, move its marker to its final red space; if not, move the Time marker to its final red space — and resolve those effects as above.

requested_parts: Whether Characters can directly attack other Characters
Whether Actions can indirectly harm other crew

answers.evidence: Characters can never directly attack other Characters (anti-aggression implants) — but they may harm them indirectly: locking someone in a burning Room, activating Self-Destruct with people aboard, throwing a Grenade into a Room with other crew, etc.

requested_parts: Procedure when an Adult must be placed but all eight Adult models are on the board

If all eight Adults are in Combat, the summary says the supply procedure is unresolved and requires authoritative clarification. 2. An Intruder entering an unexplored Room by movement stays on the board in that Room; the Room tile and Exploration token remain face down.

If all 8 Adults are in Combat, this source does not explain how to supply the required model; an authoritative clarification is needed. Intruders in unexplored Rooms: leave the Intruder miniature in that Room, on the board. The Room tile and its Exploration token both stay face down.

requested_parts: Eligible Shoot targets on the small curled Intruder symbol
Eligible Shoot targets on the larger curved Intruder symbol
Melee result against an ineligible target on either of those symbols

The larger curved symbol inflicts 1 Injury on a Larva, Creeper, or Adult and misses against a Breeder or Queen. 3. Melee has the same target-size restrictions: against an ineligible target it misses and the Character suffers 1 Serious Wound.

Larger curved Intruder symbol: 1 Injury to Larva/Creeper/Adult; miss against Breeder/Queen for Shoot. Melee has the same target restriction and 1 Injury; an ineligible target means miss and 1 Serious Wound.

requested_parts: Whether a survivor with no Larva and only non-Infected Contamination cards makes the four-card draw
Whether scanned non-Infected cards are removed
Whether an earlier launched Pod passenger still faces the Objective check
answers.answer: 1. No. With no Larva, scan every Contamination card in the Action deck, hand, and discard pile; if none is Infected, there is no four-card draw. 2. No: this endgame procedure does not remove cards merely because they scanned non-Infected. 3. Yes. Escape Pod passengers still face the final Objective check, after the Contamination check.
answers.evidence: Contamination, for every surviving Character, including launched Pod passengers: No Larva already on board: Scan every Contamination card from Action deck, hand and discard pile. If none is Infected, there is no four-card draw. This endgame procedure does not remove cards merely because they scanned non-Infected. After boarding you may launch. Remove the Pod token and its occupants' miniatures from the game; they stop participating and count as arriving on Earth. They still face the final Contamination and Objective checks. Resolve Engines → Coordinates → Contamination → Objectives in that order.

requested_parts: Antidote component symbols

Molotov Cocktail component symbols
answers.answer: 1. Antidote: flame + medical cross. 2. Taser: battery/lightning + screwdriver/tool. 3. Flamethrower: flame + screwdriver/tool. 4. Molotov Cocktail: flame + folded cloth/fabric. These are component icons to match on two Item cards, not particular Item-card names.

requested_parts: What defines being in Combat

Whether an unmarked Action or Item can be used in either situation

An In Combat Only effect can be used only while an Intruder is in the Room; an Out of Combat Only effect only while no Intruder is there. 3. An Action or Item without either marking may be used in or out of Combat, subject to its own requirements (Basic and Room Actions retain their separate limits). 4. No: Eggs do not count as Intruders and do not cause Combat.
answers.evidence: You are in Combat whenever an Intruder is in your Room. Eggs do not count as Intruders. In Combat only: you may use it only while an Intruder is in your Room. Out of Combat only: you may use it only while no Intruder is in your Room. No Combat marking on a card or Item Action: you may use it in either situation, subject to its own requirements. Basic and Room Actions retain the separate limits below.

requested_parts: Requirement for an Objective saying Player X's Character cannot survive

Regardless of Objective, your own Character must survive by escaping in a Pod or hibernating.

requested_parts: What to do if the Door-token pool is empty when a Door must be placed

requested_parts: What happens to all Escape Pods immediately after the first Character dies

A Room Action costs 2 Action cards; the Character must be in the Room whose Action is used, outside Combat, and the Room must have no Malfunction marker.

An explicit effect can give a different destination: Search and Storage keep one of two Item cards and return the other face down to the bottom of the chosen deck. Storage's Room Action works repeatedly even with its Item Counter at zero, paying the normal cost and obeying normal Room restrictions. Its counter limits only the Search Action card. requested_parts: Whether a sleeping Character takes Fire wounds from Fire appearing in the Hibernatorium

Ship destruction and endgame checks can still kill them: for example, 2 or 3 Damaged Engines explode the ship and kill hibernating Characters, non-Earth Coordinates kill an ordinary hibernating Character, and a failed Contamination check can kill a survivor.

Engines, only if the ship has survived: reveal all three top Engine tokens. 2 or 3 Damaged Engines make the ship explode. EVERYTHING aboard dies, including hibernating Characters and Intruders. Non-Earth kills hibernating Characters, while the ship is not destroyed and Intruders remain alive. Any Contamination card among those four kills you, whether Infected or not.

requested_parts: Whether Coolant Leak can start Self-Destruct while a Character is hibernating
How that differs from a Character starting it

requested_parts: Whether Fire may be placed in an unexplored Room

requested_parts: Whether reaching a later yellow Self-Destruct space unlocks Pods again after they were relocked
answers.answer: 1. No. Pods unlock automatically only when the Self-Destruct marker first reaches a yellow space; they may then be relocked, and later yellow spaces do not unlock them again.

requested_parts: Whether destroying the ship fulfills Objectives to kill the Queen or destroy the Nest
Whether fulfilling those requirements by ship destruction alone makes your Character a winner
answers.answer: 1. Yes. Ship destruction kills everything aboard, including Intruders, so it fulfills kill-the-Queen and destroy-the-Nest requirements. 2. No. Your Character must still survive and fulfill their Objective; merely satisfying the kill/destroy requirement is not sufficient to win.
answers.evidence: The Self-Destruct marker reaches the final red ("skull") space of its Track, OR you are instructed to place a 9th Fire marker, OR a 9th Malfunction marker — the ship explodes / loses hull integrity: ALL Characters on board (awake and hibernated) die, and everything else aboard dies too, including Intruders. Destruction of the ship fulfills kill-Queen/destroy-Nest requirements; your Character must still survive and fulfill their Objective (Rules 26). requested_parts: Whether a player may intentionally spend Trade with no intention of exchanging anything

requested_parts: What kind of Action activates a Quest Item

Whether a Room Malfunction prevents activation
answers.answer: 1. Activate a Quest Item with the Basic Action printed on its card; activation flips the Quest card into its active Item. 2. No. Quest activation is forbidden in Combat. 3. A Room Malfunction does not prevent activation.
answers.evidence: Each activation below is a cost-1 Basic Action, out of Combat. It flips the Quest card into its active Item; a Room Malfunction does not prevent this activation. requested_parts: Which Basic Actions are allowed in Combat

Whether an Action-card or Item Action may be used in Combat
answers.answer: 1. The Basic Actions allowed in Combat are Shoot, Melee, and Basic Movement used as Escape. 2. No: Trade, Craft, and Pick Up Heavy Object are not allowed in Combat. A card or Item marked In Combat Only is usable only while an Intruder is in your Room; an unmarked Action or Item may be used in either situation, subject to its own requirements. answers.evidence: Basic Actions in Combat are limited to Shoot, Melee and Basic Movement as Escape: no Trade, Craft, Pick Up Heavy Object or Quest Item activation. Room Actions remain forbidden (FAQ Actions 3–5). In Combat only: you may use it only while an Intruder is in your Room. Out of Combat only: you may use it only while no Intruder is in your Room. No Combat marking on a card or Item Action: you may use it in either situation, subject to its own requirements.

requested_parts: Whether Soldier may use Covering Fire for themselves alone
How direction is chosen if two Characters move
How many Noise rolls are made
Which Character's hand is used for Surprise comparison
answers.answer: 1. Yes. Soldier may use Covering Fire for themselves alone. 2. When both Characters move, each goes in a direction of their own choice. 3. They then make one Noise roll total. 4. If the roll triggers an Encounter, compare Surprise against Soldier.

requested_parts: Which Ammo is discarded and what Action follows
How the number of discarded Ammo affects damage
How the Assault Rifle bonus applies

Full Auto: remove all Ammo, perform one Shoot Action; damage adds the Shoot result, half discarded Ammo rounded down, and the Assault Rifle's +1 bonus (Actions 8).

requested_parts: When Soldier may choose Nerves of Steel relative to seeing the Intruder Attack card
Whether it can protect Soldier when another Character triggered a Surprise Attack
Whether other Characters also gain protection
answers.answer: 1. Soldier may see the Intruder Attack card before choosing it. 2. Yes. It can protect Soldier when another Character triggered a Surprise Attack. 3. Only Soldier benefits; the other Character still suffers effects directed at them, such as Frenzy.
answers.evidence: Nerves of Steel: you may see the Intruder Attack card before choosing it. It can protect Soldier when another Character triggered a Surprise Attack, but only Soldier benefits; other Characters still take effects such as Frenzy (Actions 9–10).

requested_parts: Effect of Careful Movement on an automatic Danger or Silence Exploration result
